title: PTWC threshold detection depended on one record in 7 of 24 reached regions with at least six records in 2014-2026
abstract: We audit a fixed archive of first PTWC threat categories and tide-gauge records. Of 33 threat pairs with at least six records, 24 reached the stated lower threshold. Seven of these 24 pairs had only one record that reached it. Exact random withholding accounts for 85.5% of the dense-sparse reach gap (event-bootstrap 95% interval 72.0-96.6%). At one record per pair, dense regions still have a 10.3 percentage point higher reach rate (3.7-20.1). Within seven shared earthquakes, this difference is 5.0 points (-2.0 to 12.9), so event selection remains a plausible source. Duplicate coordinates do not change the result. These tests support a large sampling effect, but do not identify coastal calibration. Without restrictions on unobserved coastlines, the coastal threshold reach rate is bounded only by 30.9-100% in observed pairs and 19.4-100% in all threat pairs. We provide exact finite-record detection tools, code, source hashes, aggregate results and a reproduction recipe. The study reuses the prior archive and is not an independent forecast validation.

display.caption: Exact detection under random record withholding and the dense-sparse comparison at equal effort. Bands are 95% event-bootstrap intervals.

citations.reason: Reuse the fixed archive and region rules; quantify finite-record detection and limits on coastal inference.
